Round 3 appended.

**[2.1] is resolved.** `diff final/p1.tex output/p1/answer.tex` and `diff final/p2.tex output/p2/answer.tex` are both empty. I checked the *direction* of the merge rather than just equality — the surviving text is the fixed wording ("Five transition rules… giving the seven configurations", both disclosed `comparison_table()` captions), not a revert to the round-1 phrasing. And I proved the idempotence claim myself rather than taking the master's log for it, since that's the property whose absence caused the defect: re-assembling from the worker deliverables reproduces `final/` exactly, and I independently re-derived `preamble.tex` as the de-duplicated union of the two worker preambles (9 packages, exact match). A future re-assembly can no longer silently revert anything.

**Nothing else moved.** All four `.tex` sources are byte-identical to the round-2 versions I already validated, and the shipped `main.pdf`'s extracted text is identical to round 2's with zero differences. So round 1's correctness work carries over untouched and re-running the experiments wasn't warranted. I did rebuild the document from the shipped sources to confirm the shipped PDF is actually the product of those sources and not a stale artefact — rc=0, 14 pages, zero overfull boxes, and my rebuild's text matches exactly. Figures are md5-identical between each worker dir and `final/`, lint passes on both worker dirs, and the full OUTPUT inventory is 17 files with no aux, log or scratch anywhere.

The master's fix also addressed the root cause by adding the idempotence check to its own assembly procedure, not just this instance.

Across three rounds I reproduced three full experiment runs bit-exactly, recomputed every dataset statistic and derived ratio from the raw data, re-ran the corpus accounting, sampler type-correctness gates, rare-artist measurement and cold-start coverage, checked the load-bearing assortativity claim (87.5% same-country edges vs 11.9% at chance), and read the document through both channels. Coverage is complete against the assignment as I enumerated it from the source. I found no number in the document that disagrees with what the code produces, and I have nothing substantive left to blame.

VERDICT: PASS
